# jsonstor-mongodb

> Home: [http://jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com)
>
> Version: 0.1.0

### Documents are stored on a MongoDB server.

Overview
---------------------------------------------------------------------

`jsonstor` defines one interface for working with a document store and implements it
  for a variety of database products and file formats. The interface is the same whichever
  adapter is underneath, so the storage a project uses becomes a configuration decision
  rather than a structural one.

This package is one such adapter. Documents are stored on a MongoDB server.

***It is packaged separately so that it stays optional.*** A project which does not store
  documents this way never downloads [`mongodb`](https://github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native).

See [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) for the interface,
  and [jsonstor.liquicode.com](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com) for the documentation.

Getting Started
---------------------------------------------------------------------

```bash
npm install --save @liquicode/jsonstor-mongodb
```

```js
const jsonstor = require( '@liquicode/jsonstor' )();
jsonstor.LoadPlugin( require( '@liquicode/jsonstor-mongodb' ) );

let storage = jsonstor.GetStorage( 'jsonstor-mongodb', {
	ConnectionString: '...',
	DatabaseName: '...',
	CollectionName: '...',
} );
```

Settings
---------------------------------------------------------------------

| Setting | Required | Default | Description |
|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| `ConnectionString` | ***Yes*** | - | The MongoDB connection string, e.g. `mongodb://localhost`. |
| `DatabaseName` | ***Yes*** | - | The name of the database to use. |
| `CollectionName` | ***Yes*** | - | The name of the collection to use. |

Peculiarities
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- ***This adapter is the reference the others are measured against.*** `jsonstor` establishes what correct means by running the shared inventory through this adapter against a live server, and comparing every other storage to that result. Where they disagree, the other adapter is wrong.
- ***Criteria are handed to the MongoDB driver, not to `jsongin`.*** The operators a query may use are the operators the server implements, which is why this adapter is the baseline rather than a participant.
- The database and the collection are created on the first storage call if they do not exist.
- All three settings are required, and the adapter throws if any is missing or is not a string.

Storage Interface
---------------------------------------------------------------------

Every adapter implements the same functions, and they are documented once:
  [Storage Interface](http://jsonstor.liquicode.com/#/guides/Storage%20Interface.md).

***The operator list is not repeated here.*** A criteria, a projection, and an update are
  the engine's, and the list changes whenever the engine gains an operator - a copy in this
  file could only ever be out of date. See the
  [Operator Reference](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin/blob/main/docs/guides/Operator-Reference.md).

Dependencies
---------------------------------------------------------------------

- [`mongodb`](https://github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native) : The official MongoDB driver for Node.
- [`@liquicode/jsonstor`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsonstor) : The storage interface.
- [`@liquicode/jsongin`](https://github.com/liquicode/jsongin) : The query engine.
